newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF head, Russia discussed opening gas exploration.
newsitem.headline: IMF head, Russia discussed opening gas exploration.

text.p: The head of the International Monetary Fund said on Wednesday he had discussed opening natural gas exploration to firms other than monopolist Gazprom with top Russian government officials.

Michel Camdessus told students at an international affairs institute that he had discussed a programme which "includes opening...gas exploration for companies other than Gazprom" with First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov and other officials.
Gazprom produces nearly 100 percent of Russian natural gas and does not allow the few tiny, independent Russian producers that exist, to have access to its pipelines.
It is the largest natural gas producer in the world, and although government leaders have spoken favourably of it, they have said that it must be reformed.
Nemtsov was appointed minister recently by President Boris Yeltsin and charged with leading natural monopoly reform.

Camdessus is in Moscow for talks with senior Russian ministers on resuming disbursements of a de-facto suspended $10 billion three-year loan and agreeing an economic programme for 1997 to be backed by the loan.
Camdessus said now was the time for the international community to resuming financing to Russia.
